summary: The Monday arXiv announcement adds a tightly connected light-ion package: ALICE multi-particle flow measurements in OO and Ne-Ne collisions and a theory study showing that orientational averaging conventions can materially shift inferred Ne-20 eccentricities. A fragmentation energy correlator broadens spin-sensitive QCD measurements across collision systems. In AI/ML, FeynFacet is the strongest contribution because it couples agent-written symbolic programs to extensive analytic and physical validation; a seven-model PDE benchmark gives an important warning that short-horizon accuracy can hide large autoregressive error growth.
professional_summary: Light-ion geometry, multi-particle flow, fragmentation energy correlators, validated agent-assisted NLO QCD, long-horizon PDE-surrogate reliability, and amortized simulator-based design dominate the selected papers.
strongest_paper: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
strongest_paper_summary: Agent-developed symbolic programs reproduce several established NLO QCD calculations and pass gauge-invariance, pole-cancellation, and RG checks before producing new transverse-spin-transfer hard functions.

papers.title: Anisotropic flow measurements in OO and Ne-Ne collisions with ALICE
papers.short_authors: Vojtech Machacek for the ALICE Collaboration
papers.abstract: ALICE reports charged-particle anisotropic flow in OO and Ne-Ne collisions using cumulants through eight particles, reconstructs P(v2), and measures v3{4}/v3{2} in light-ion systems.
papers.summary: Using about 3 billion OO and 410 million Ne-Ne minimum-bias events at 5.36 TeV, ALICE measures v2 through eight-particle cumulants plus v3 and v4. The larger mean v2 and non-Bessel-Gaussian triangular-flow fluctuations in Ne-Ne are consistent with a stronger imprint of the deformed Ne-20 geometry.
papers.why_it_matters: These are direct, high-statistics constraints on how known nuclear geometry propagates into collective flow in systems small enough to stress hydrodynamic interpretations.
papers.assessment: Scientifically important and experimentally careful, with subevent suppression of nonflow and systematic variations. The public paper is only a four-page proceedings contribution, however; higher-order cumulants remain statistically limited and quantitative nuclear-structure inference awaits a full analysis.

papers.title: Orientational average in nuclear shape imaging: densities, correlations, and eccentricity in Ne-20
papers.short_authors: Jian Deng, Hao-jie Xu, Qun Wang
papers.abstract: A deformed harmonic-oscillator model compares rigid-rotor and wave-function-rotor orientational averaging for Ne-20 densities, pair correlations, multipoles, and ultracentral eccentricity variances.
papers.summary: The two orientation prescriptions yield different laboratory radial moments, pair correlations, beta20, beta40, and eccentricity variances at fixed deformation. Several internal scaling relations remain similar, but the absolute mapping from intrinsic deformation to collision geometry is prescription dependent.
papers.why_it_matters: The result identifies a structural theory uncertainty that sits directly between nuclear wave functions and the light-ion flow observables now measured by ALICE.
papers.assessment: A timely and technically clear diagnostic. Its quantitative conclusions are model dependent: the study uses a deformed harmonic oscillator and a leading-order ultracentral mapping rather than a full event-by-event collision and hydrodynamic calculation.

papers.title: A universal probe of QCD spin physics from fragmentation energy correlator
papers.short_authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Xiaohui Liu, Zhite Yu, C.-P. Yuan, Feng Yuan, Shu-Tao Zhang, Hua Xing Zhu
papers.abstract: The fragmentation energy correlator combines a nonperturbative fragmentation function with an infrared-safe energy correlator and is formulated for lepton-lepton, lepton-hadron, and hadron-hadron collisions.
papers.summary: The authors argue that the observable accesses transverse-spin-dependent hadronization without jet finding or a tagged heavy object. Its scale dependence is proposed as a probe of the chiral-symmetry-breaking scale and is supported by theoretical derivation and numerical studies.
papers.why_it_matters: A common observable across e+e-, EIC, RHIC, and LHC environments could make universality tests of spin-dependent fragmentation substantially cleaner.
papers.assessment: Conceptually strong and broadly useful, but its direct heavy-ion payoff is prospective. Experimental feasibility, backgrounds, detector effects, and medium modifications still need dedicated studies before universality can be tested in nuclear collisions.

papers.title: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
papers.short_authors: Zhong-Bo Kang, Werner Vogelsang, Congyue Zhang
papers.abstract: AI agents develop and execute process-specific symbolic programs for analytic NLO QCD, producing new transverse-spin-transfer hard functions after reproducing known collinear and TMD results.
papers.summary: FeynFacet links amplitude generation, reverse unitarity, IBP reduction, dimensional shifts, and analytic integration. It reproduces established unpolarized and polarized hard functions plus TMD matching and soft coefficients, then derives new proton-proton and lepton-proton transverse-spin-transfer results.
papers.use_case: The workflow could accelerate auditable fixed-order calculations for RHIC, EIC, and LHC observables, especially spin and fragmentation quantities whose conventions and evanescent terms make manual algebra fragile.
papers.assessment: The day's strongest AI paper. The claim is backed by unusually rich checks: independent algebra systems, known-result reproduction, gauge invariance, pole cancellation, RG evolution, and released programs. It remains a physicist-supervised workflow, not evidence of autonomous trustworthy theory production.

papers.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: Benchmarking the Rollout Reliability of PDE Foundation Models
papers.short_authors: Jaewan Park, Seid Koric, Giri Krishnan, Sudhakar Pamidighantam, Surresh Marru
papers.abstract: Seven learned PDE models are evaluated on seven two-dimensional time-dependent datasets with paired short- and full-horizon rollout metrics.
papers.summary: Foundation-model recipes often retain a relative advantage over scratch baselines, yet full-horizon error exceeds short-horizon error in 140 of 144 paired configurations, with median amplification 2.04. The study argues for horizon-resolved absolute errors and explicit failure counts rather than one local forecast score.
papers.use_case: Heavy-ion hydrodynamic emulators and plasma-transport surrogates are autoregressive dynamical systems; this benchmark design is directly transferable to validating them before inference or event-generation use.
papers.assessment: A strong evaluation paper with broad physics relevance and commendably explicit limitations. It compares end-to-end recipes rather than isolating pretraining, uses only 2D grid simulations, and does not test experimental noise, 3D dynamics, conservation-law violations, or heavy-ion equations specifically.

papers.title: Amortized Thompson Sampling and Efficient Information-Directed Sampling for Simulator-Based Design
papers.abstract: A learned amortized approximation makes multi-round Thompson sampling and expected-information-gain estimation efficient for implicit simulator-based design.
papers.summary: The method trains before observations arrive so that posterior-dependent design recommendations can be produced cheaply across sequential rounds. Combining expected information gain with immediate regret enables information-directed sampling, demonstrated on two likelihood-intractable synthetic-biology simulators.
papers.use_case: The same machinery could prioritize costly detector simulations, beam-time configurations, calibration scans, or theory parameter points when each simulator call is expensive and the likelihood is unavailable.
papers.assessment: Methodologically credible and potentially useful, but transfer to HEP is not established. Evidence is limited to two synthetic-biology tasks; robustness to high-dimensional collider observations, severe simulator misspecification, and coverage constraints remains open.
